scores.evidence: Gapless sequence per legal entity, allocated at finalization inside the ledger transaction (not at draft)
scores.rationale: Technical claims are accurate and precise throughout the subtle areas (SAQ A via PSP-hosted fields, outbox for side effects, at-least-once ingest with dedupe, append-only ledger, gapless numbering at finalization), with legal and vendor claims cited or flagged for confirmation.

scores.evidence: If instead we offer billing-as-a-service (tenants bill *their* customers), there is a second tenancy level
scores.rationale: It resolves the request's central ambiguity explicitly, covers every core billing capability, is credibly phased for one team, and defers non-essentials with stated pull-forward triggers.

scores.evidence: Ledger, invoices, and payments are strongly consistent (single primary, serializable posting). Ingest favors availability
scores.rationale: Consistency, identity, tenancy and error-propagation choices are made once and honored everywhere (money strongly consistent, usage at-least-once with dedupe, entitlements eventually consistent), with clear data ownership and no contradictions.

scores.evidence: 10k test-mode charges with worker kills, PSP timeouts, webhook replays; a synthetic anomaly run; refund drill
scores.rationale: V0–V9 tie checkable thresholds to the specific risks, validate the riskiest decisions early (build-vs-buy, isolation, ledger invariants before invoicing, 2-cycle shadow before any charge), and continue in production via invariant monitors, reconciliation and per-wave gates.

scores.evidence: The plan proceeds on these assumptions; each one changes the plan if false
scores.rationale: Every number is labeled ASSUMPTION, UNKNOWN or REQUIREMENT with an owner to confirm it, and the plan states which assumptions restructure the phases if wrong.

scores.evidence: injected duplicates, reordering, late events, and consumer crashes
scores.rationale: Covers the hard domain failures — double charges, cross-tenant leaks, duplicate/late/reordered events, webhook replays, runaway invoice runs, restore/DR — with concrete detection (invariant monitor, reconciliation, breaker) and recovery (credit note + refund, cohort rollback); only dispute/chargeback handling is thin.

scores.evidence: ≤ 3 deployables (ingest, billing core, workers) + Postgres + one stream, on the existing platform on-call rotation
scores.rationale: Deploy/rollback is rehearsed in Phase 0, migrations are expand/contract, meaningful signals (ledger invariants, reconciliation, dedupe rates) are monitored, on-call staffing gates exposure, and an explicit operational-complexity budget sizes it to one team.
The dominant cost trade-off (vendor fees vs build) is handled rigorously in V1 and storage retention/compaction is costed, but running-cost growth with usage and engineering-time estimates are thin.

scores.evidence: the seam keeps code rework to R2; it doesn't make tokens portable
scores.rationale: Every key decision carries an explicit reversibility class, revisit trigger and exit path (PSP card-data export clause, cell migration, cohort rollback), the point of no return is isolated to Phase 7 behind V9, and it is honest about what the adapter seam does not buy.

scores.evidence: Second currency or selling entity: the data model supports both from Phase 1; enabling either waits for the first sale
scores.rationale: Each component is justified by a stated need, speculative scale (cells, sharding, ClickHouse, CPQ) is deferred with concrete pull-forward triggers, and no essential is dropped.

scores.evidence: The product backend emits one real usage event (`api_calls: 1`) for the company's own internal dogfood tenant
scores.rationale: A concrete first slice, dependency-ordered phases with checkable exit criteria, specific decisions (ULIDs, 72 h late window, idempotency key scheme), and an 'if it fails' branch for every validation make this immediately executable.

checklist.evidence: Money as integer minor units plus ISO currency
Append-only double-entry ledger. Prices are immutable and versioned. Corrections are credit notes, never edits.
Charge executor with idempotency key = invoice ID + attempt
No card number (PAN) ever touches our systems; PSP-hosted fields only, so scope is SAQ A
Postgres row-level security (RLS) enforced for the app role
Dedupe and late-arrival window (design parameter: 72 h)
Subscription lifecycle: create, upgrade, downgrade, cancel, proration
EU VAT requires sequential numbering (Directive 2006/112/EC Art. 226)
100% of ledger payment entries matched to PSP settlement daily; unmatched items resolved within 1 business day
entitlement cache on a billing outage → fail open with last-known state for tenants in good standing
Model every current plan and every plan on the 12-month roadmap in Stripe Billing and one usage-billing vendor sandbox

traps.evidence: Money as integer minor units plus ISO currency
Corrections are credit notes, never edits
No card number (PAN) ever touches our systems; PSP-hosted fields only
every API and job uses tenant-A credentials against tenant-B IDs; RLS bypass attempts

note: An exemplary plan that avoids every domain trap, validates its riskiest decisions early with checkable gates, and labels every assumption; only subscription edge cases (trials, pauses, billing anchors), dunning policy detail, and run-cost estimation fall short.
